sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Boga language [bvw] (Internet Archive copy 2025-05-22).
sources.note: Only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries; no language descriptions, no primary data archived.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2024. Ethnologue, 27th ed.: Boga [bvw] (free view, Internet Archive copy 2024-08-01).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Free view gives only vitality/population (10K-1M, stable); no typology or phonology text; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT (PhD, Leiden).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Boga: the data-source table (p. 12, pdf p. 40) reads 'Boga [bvw] Tera none', i.e. no lexical/phonological data for Boga were available; Boga is placed in East Tera with Ga'anda and Hwana (p. 49-50). Family-wide: 'No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress' (p. 229) and 'Studies in the development of Central Chadic tone systems are at a very early stage' (p. 86).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition (version 03 December 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry '50. Boga / 1.A Boka / 3. Adamawa State, Gombi LGA / 5. Chadic: Biu-Mandara branch A: Tera group: Eastern Cluster / Source(s) S. Lukas wordlist / Refs. Newman (1964) fn.4' (p. 12) and '134. Boga.. 4. 5 villages' (p. 27): the only sources it knows are an unpublished Lukas wordlist and a footnote in Newman 1964; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (n.d.) Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Boga (data supplied by Charles H. Kraft, 18 July 2007).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Numerals 1-100 with tone marks (ɨrtà, cə̀p, məkkən, fwəɗà..); says only that Boga has a decimal system; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, vol. II (Biu-Mandara). Berlin: Dietrich Reimer — 'Boka' list as digitised in the CLDF dataset lexibank/kraftchadic.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only (437 Boka forms); forms carry tone diacritics (451 combining grave accents, 35 circumflexes, no acutes), showing Kraft transcribed Boga as tonal, but the derivative contains no prose on tone or stress; Kraft's introductory volume with transcription conventions was not accessible.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Biu-Mandara languages' (Tera group section; Boga numerals cited from Chan).
sources.note: Boga listed as East Tera, Gombi LGA, 5 villages; numerals with tone marks; nothing on stress.
